subject: Recap: Reliability & graceful degradation — FinOps discovery
messages:
From: Aisha Sharma <aisha@finops.co>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-07T18:32:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up: reliability pain & incident history

Ben / Monica,

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick summary from our side (so you have context for a pilot):

Incident history (last 6 months):
- Jul 14: us-east-1 partial region outage -> ~4 hours of degraded throughput, retries caused downstream queueing.
- Sep 03: model rollout (1.3B -> 13B variant) introduced a 2–3x latency tail under burst, spiking token cost.
- Oct 27: retry storm after a transient DB timeout increased upstream traffic and caused backpressure.

Primary pain points:
- Unpredictable tail latency during peak windows (affects UX SLAs)
- No automated fallback to cheaper/robust model variants when high latency detected
- Cost spikes from retries and inefficient batching during incidents

Success criteria for a pilot (what we agreed):
- Median inference latency <= 50ms for short (<=128 token) RPCs
- 99.5% availability for the inference API during business hours
- Clear, measurable unit-cost improvement (target: <= 0.8x current $/token under baseline workload)

Can you send a concise post-call recap with proposed fallback strategies and a short mutual action plan? Also include any templates for SLOs you recommend.

Thanks,
Aisha Sharma
CTO, FinOps Co
[Attachment: incident-summary-Q3.pdf (pdf)]

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Sharma <aisha@finops.co>, Kara Lee <kara.lee@finops.co>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-07T21:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: reliability pain & incident history

Hi Aisha / Kara — thanks for the clear notes. Appreciate the specifics on the incidents; that helps scope the pilot. Below is a concise recap of what we discussed and a proposed action plan focused on reliability and graceful degradation.

Recap — observed pain & root causes (as discussed):
- Tail latency spikes: primarily during model rollouts and burst windows; related to model size and KV cache misses.
- Lack of automated fallback: no circuit-breaker or model-variant fallback in place -> retries route to same heavy variant.
- Retry storms amplify cost and pressure on upstream systems.

Proposed graceful-degradation strategy (high level):
1) Model-variant fallback chain: primary (13B quantized) -> warm standby (7B int8) -> tiny fallback (3B quantized) for critical low-latency paths. Auto-failover triggered by latency thresholds + error budget consumption.
2) Regional failover: prefer regional routing (us-east primary, us-west hot-standby). Use health-based routing + automatic KV cache warming on failover to reduce cold-start penalty.
3) Circuit breakers & backpressure: short-circuit expensive dynamic reranks when downstream signals indicate overload; respond with cached/bounded outputs for non-critical routes.
4) Batching & cache tuning: prefix caching for common prompts + adaptive batching limits during normal windows; aggressive caching during failover.
5) Canary release + staged rollouts: model changes pushed via canary on 5% traffic, automatic rollback on quality/latency regression signals.

Suggested SLOs / SLAs for pilot:
- Availability: 99.5% monthly for inference endpoint (business-hours baseline)
- Latency: P50 <= 50ms, P95 <= 220ms for <=128 token requests (we can tune P95 target during pilot)
- Error budget: 0.5% monthly
- Escalation SLA: 2 business-hour response for Sev2, 30-minute on-call for Sev1 (can map to credits in a production SLA)

Pilot scope & deliverables (6 weeks recommended):
- Week 1: Baseline instrumentation (tail latency histograms, cache hit metrics, model variant metrics)
- Week 2–3: Implement fallback chain & regional routing in staging; dry-run failovers
- Week 4: Canary rollout policy enforcement + monitoring dashboards
- Week 5–6: Production pilot on dedicated capacity (low volume) + runbook for fallback operations

Immediate next steps (actionable):
- Ill share a short SLO worksheet and an architecture sketch for the fallback flow (attached).
- Can you confirm the preferred pilot region (us-east preferred per call) and a point of contact for procurement (email)?
- Well schedule a technical onboarding with one of our solutions engineers to size the dedicated pool and the KV cache parameters.

Attachments included: FinOps-SLO-worksheet.xlsx, redwood-fallback-arch.png, mutual-action-plan.docx

If that captures it, Ill convert this into a short mutual action plan and a DocuSign/PO checklist for procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
